Assistant A's response is completely incorrect. It claims to implement a solution for arrays of different sizes, but then explicitly raises a `ValueError` if the arrays are not the same length. It also claims that sorting arrays (which takes $O(n \log n)$) results in $O(n)$ time complexity, and the logic used to find the median is mathematically wrong.

Assistant B correctly identifies that the problem can be solved even more efficiently than $O(n)$ (specifically $O(\log(\min(n, m)))$) and provides a correct, industry-standard implementation of the binary search approach for finding the median of two sorted arrays. While Assistant B claims it is "not possible" to do it in $O(n)$ (which is technically incorrect, as a simple two-pointer merge-style traversal would achieve $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ space), the provided solution is superior in both correctness and efficiency.

[[B]]
